purpose: Electron desktop cockpit for driving Claude Code CLI sessions across projects via a TAB→Epic→PRD hierarchy, with scheduling, chat/terminal views, and mobile relay.
what: The core domain model is **TAB = project cwd**, **EPIC = tagged claude session** (`PromptSession`) with a strict `proposed → active → completed` lifecycle, and **PRD** = scheduler work items minted under an Epic. Recent commits (`b2b1b82`, `92280db`, `3d12e19`) hardened this invariant so nothing can mint an Epic directly into `active` and `active-index.json` writes are read-merge-write, not blind overwrites.

A **single-writer law** (`opsOwnership.cjs`) governs `session-manager-operations/<namespace>/` — each namespace has exactly one owning surface, fail-closed on violation. `feedback/` intake is fully retired in favor of `status: 'proposed'` Epics as the human-approval gate.

Recent work (v0.47–v0.53) focused on **nav consolidation** (merging Scheduler's Home/Project faces, distinct Home-tab vs Project-tab left-nav, dropping redundant horizontal tabs), **Epic Queue UX** (single Actions menu, Build toolbar button, discuss-first path), and a **Canvas-2 Scheduler redesign** (`f559d59`) plus **Epic UI audit** driven by Claude-Code-Design-MCP mocks.
`v51 Perf Issues` (slow tab-switching, suspected memory leaks) was addressed in `3e72cb1` alongside epic-creation review-gate fixes, landed together in the v0.53.0 release.

**Project Pages** is a newer subsystem (`projectPages.cjs`, `projectBrief.cjs`) — a static-HTML component-library renderer with deterministic variant selection (Stage 2) and summary validation (Stage 3/4), built out across several `feat(project-pages)` commits.

scope: No 'general' OWNERS namespace — architecture/design-mocks/HUMAN_LEARN/reviews stay outside single-writer law as skill-authored documentation, not app-owned runtime state
conventions: Epic status has exactly 3 states (proposed/active/completed); never create directly as 'active' — enforced structurally now in ensureEpic and createPromptSession.
Single-writer law: every ops namespace has one owner; cross-writer needs a declared delegation, not ad-hoc fs writes.
Scheduler cap of ≤3 concurrent `claude -p` sessions (session slot pool) — do not raise casually; a related Epic requested making this configurable 0-10 (default 5).
Zustand selectors must never return a freshly-built reference (three prior blank-app incidents) — guarded by `npm run lint:selectors`.
Nav destinations are deduped as independent 'micro-services' — extend an existing surface (e.g. Scheduler) before adding a new LeftNav tab.
